# `run_item_series`

> **GENERATED** — rendered from the data contract. Edit [`supabase/contract/run_item_series.contract.yaml`](../../../supabase/contract/run_item_series.contract.yaml)

**Tier 5** — results — pinned to dataset + policy + engine version · owned by `engine` · `public.run_item_series`

**One row is** One item's weekly series from one INSPECTION run: a material or a product of the project, and a map of named weekly arrays for it (on-hand, in-transit and orders for a material; demand, production, fulfillment, backlog and lost units for a product). Written ONLY for an inspection run — exactly one replication, user-chosen seed, engine trace raised to full debug — because per-item evidence at multi-replication scale is deliberately not exposed; every other run has no rows here. Tier 5 — a RESULT of one run, input to nothing; a row is superseded by re-running, never edited.

## Uniqueness

| `run_id` + `kind` + `item_id` | UNIQUE index | `run_item_series_run_kind_item_uq` |

**Natural key:** `run_id` + `kind` + `item_id` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `run_item_series_run_kind_item_uq`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `simulation_lab` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | **no** — invariant `audit-actor` is not met here yet |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — **2 with no predicate** |

`write: simulation_lab` because the table has two PREDICATE-LESS write policies — `run_item_series_auth_all` (authenticated) and `run_item_series_anon_write` (anon and authenticated, widened by WP 7.1 stage 1a in `20260919000010`) — and a policy with no predicate is a user-facing write path whether or not a page uses it, so `governanceEnforcement.test.ts` refuses a `null` claim here exactly as it did for `run_replications`. The capability named is the one that gates the action which writes these rows: running a simulation, here an inspection run from Run & Validate. TWO WRITERS, both upserting on `(run_id, kind, item_id)` in chunks of 100: the Fly worker with the service role (`_write_item_series`, which FAILS the run rather than reporting it green when the rows do not persist), and the browser engine as `anon` (`pyodideEngine.persistEngineResult`, best-effort). The second is why this is one of the eleven tables §4 D154 measured as genuinely writable from the browser's `anon` role — D28's standing decision (document, do not change), WP 7.1's to close. `min_project_role` is `viewer` because nothing here enforces a role today, not because a viewer ought to be able to write results. Deleting the run or the project removes its rows (`ON DELETE CASCADE` on both foreign keys). NOT AUDITED, and that is the tier: `audit-actor` covers tiers 2–4, and a row here is the output of one run and an input to nothing.

> **What the database actually permits is wider than the row above.**
> 2 policies here grant access with
> **no predicate at all** (`USING (true)`), so the capability named above is what the
> product intends to check, not what the database enforces:
>
> - `run_item_series_auth_all` — `ALL` to `authenticated`
> - `run_item_series_anon_write` — `ALL` to `anon`, `authenticated`
>
> Some of these permit **writes**. See PLAN.md D28: the application runs as the
> `anon` role with no auth session and the anon key ships in the frontend bundle, so
> closing these is a migration with an auth model behind it rather than a policy edit.

| `series` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | The item's weekly series, one array per measure, each as long as the run's horizon in weeks. The measures are the engine's per-item trace matrices, declared once as the `item_series` dict in scsim/scsim/core/engine.py and keyed `<kind>.<measure>` there; this column carries the part after the dot. Every measure is in units of the item. `unit_source` is `derived` because some measures are stocks (on hand, in transit, backlog) and some are weekly flows (orders, demand, production, fulfillment, lost units), and that follows from the measure, not from one token for the column. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the row was first inserted. An upsert of the same key does not re-stamp it. |

### `series`

The item's weekly series, one array per measure, each as long as the run's horizon in weeks. The measures are the engine's per-item trace matrices, declared once as the `item_series` dict in scsim/scsim/core/engine.py and keyed `<kind>.<measure>` there; this column carries the part after the dot. Every measure is in units of the item. `unit_source` is `derived` because some measures are stocks (on hand, in transit, backlog) and some are weekly flows (orders, demand, production, fulfillment, lost units), and that follows from the measure, not from one token for the column.

| | |
|---|---|
| Type | `jsonb`, `NOT NULL`, default `'{}'::jsonb` |
| Grain | `level` |
| Unit | none recorded (derived) |
| Added by | `20260720000001_run_item_series.sql` |
| Read by the engine | `scsim_bridge.py::compute_run_from_project -> item_series[].series` |
| Transform | one row per (kind, item) of each item_series matrix; _finite(x, 5) per element, so NaN and ±inf become null |
| Validated at ingest | — |
| Rendered at | `[object Object]`, `[object Object]` |

**Rendered on** `ProjectPolicies.tsx` (`src/components/sim/ItemSeriesExplorer.tsx:118`), `SimulationLab.tsx` (`src/components/sim/ItemSeriesExplorer.tsx:118`) —
each of these names this column in an explicit `select` list, so the claim
is about the column and not only about the table.

> The explorer's legend names the measures for display; it is a label map, not a second declaration, and a measure it does not know still renders under its key. The migration's header comment also lists them — written when the table was created and not maintained since, so the engine is the authority. NO `computed_by`, for `run_replications`' reason: the producer is scsim (Python, in the Fly worker or in Pyodide), which `contract:check` R18 cannot resolve; `engine.consumed_by` carries the path instead. DEFAULT `'{}'` — a row whose series is empty is a row the engine produced no measures for, not a row of zeros.
